analysis.title: Everyone Sold The Lows. Now The Squeeze Is On
key_insights: Tech reversed from panic selling to FOMO buying within days. NDX futures are back above the 200-day MA after bouncing off a major long-term trendline and returning to the familiar range.

SPX is back above the midpoint of its range and above the 200-day MA. The house theme is to trade the range (buy lows, sell highs), but many players did the opposite, selling the lows and chasing the squeeze higher.

Semiconductors are roughly 25% below YTD highs but up nearly 20% from the recent lows. AMD is up 40% in four sessions, with limited participation from NVDA. The debate is high-beta, high-gross-margin names versus quality.

UBS estimates CTA global equity exposure at -5%, the 5th percentile over the past year and 23rd percentile over five years, down from a peak near +150% earlier in the cycle. A sustained rebound could force CTAs to rebuy equities.
Vol-control funds slashed exposure as volatility rose (Nomura). If volatility keeps drifting lower, the vol-control bid returns and adds to the rally.
The VIX overshoot during Thursday's crash has normalized and the gap between VIX and SPX is basically closed.
BofA says the one-month performance spread between defensives and technology is at extremes last seen in the dotcom era, leaving the defensive trade vulnerable to a sharp reversal if tech rebounds.

China has added $5 trillion to GDP since Covid but its equities have underperformed global markets by 110 percentage points. Goldman sees 10% trend earnings growth and 10-15% potential valuation upside, and several key China indices are stabilizing around technical levels.

Silver positioning has been reset: Goldman reports $2.3B of cumulative non-dealer selling over the four weeks into November 3, driven by $2.6B of new shorts partly offset by $300M of long buying. Net speculative length is at the 2nd percentile of the past two years in notional terms.

Silver's three-month normalized 25-delta put-call skew has retreated from its highest levels since COVID (Goldman), showing downside-protection demand is unwinding while silver stays vulnerable to sharp two-way moves.

market_movers.rationale: AMD rose 40% in four sessions during the semiconductor rebound, while NVDA participated only to a limited degree.

sector_views.rationale: Sector is about 25% below YTD highs and up nearly 20% from recent lows. The note frames it as a bear-market bounce versus mid-cycle correction debate without committing.
Positioning washout, CTA short exposure and collapsing volatility set up another squeeze higher in tech.
The defensive-versus-tech performance spread is at dotcom-era extremes, so the next pain trade could be defensives underperforming.

trade_ideas.rationale: The market remains mean-reverting, and players who sold lows and chased highs did the opposite.
